balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For TCL Electronics Holdings Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For TCL Electronics Holdings Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For TCL Electronics Holdings Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For TCL Electronics Holdings Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For TCL Electronics Holdings Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For TCL Electronics Holdings Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For TCL Electronics Holdings Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For TCL Electronics Holdings Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For TCL Electronics Holdings Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

segmentRevenue.title: Revenue by segment
segmentRevenue.content:
TCL Electronics splits revenue into large display (TV sets, the core business), internet (smart-TV advertising and content services), innovative business (other consumer electronics) and photovoltaic (solar, the newest diversification).

For TCL Electronics Holdings Limited: large display is still roughly half of revenue, but internet and photovoltaic carry structurally higher gross margins -- the mix shift toward them is the re-rating case, not TV unit growth alone.

What to watch:

  • Large-display share of revenue trending down as internet/photovoltaic scale
  • Photovoltaic revenue, a new and currently volatile line, versus the more mature internet segment
  • Segment data is only disclosed annually and in H1 filings since FY2024, so early years show gaps

segmentMargin.title: Internet vs large-display gross margin
segmentMargin.content:
Internet gross margin (advertising and content services on TCL's smart-TV operating system) versus large-display gross margin (hardware).

For TCL Electronics Holdings Limited: internet gross margin runs well above 50% versus large-display margin in the mid-teens -- the segment-mix chart above shows volume, this one shows why the mix matters for blended profitability.

What to watch:

  • Internet margin holding up as the advertising business scales
  • Large-display margin under pressure from panel costs and competition

tvShipments.title: TV shipments and Mini LED mix
tvShipments.content:
TV shipments is total unit volume shipped; Mini LED TV shipments is the premium-tier subset using Mini LED backlighting.

For TCL Electronics Holdings Limited: TCL competes on volume (top-3 global TV shipments) but Mini LED is the premiumization lever -- rising Mini LED mix should lift large-display gross margin even if total unit shipments are flat.

What to watch:

  • Mini LED mix rising as a share of total shipments
  • Unit shipments growing faster or slower than large-display revenue (price/mix effect)
  • Only disclosed annually; not every year has a Mini LED figure

tvMarketShare.title: Global TV market share
tvMarketShare.content:
Share by shipment volume and share by revenue are management's disclosed global TV market-share estimates (third-party industry data, e.g. Omdia/AVC).

For TCL Electronics Holdings Limited: share by revenue running below share by shipment volume confirms TCL sells at a lower average selling price than the market -- consistent with its volume-led, value-segment strategy versus premium rivals.

What to watch:

  • Share by revenue closing the gap with share by shipment as Mini LED mix rises
  • Only disclosed annually, and only for the two most recent years

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For TCL Electronics Holdings Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
